subject: biology
promptStrong: Give me an exam-style {board} {level} {subject} question on {lo}, then mark my answer against the mark scheme.
promptWeak: Explain {lo} for {board} {level} {subject} simply, with a clear example and the most common mistake students make.

questions.q: Which structure is found in a plant cell but NOT in an animal cell?
questions.explain: Plant cells have a cellulose cell wall for support, whereas animal cells do not.

questions.q: In a prokaryotic cell such as a bacterium, the genetic material is:
options: A single loop of DNA free in the cytoplasm
questions.explain: Prokaryotes have no nucleus; their DNA is a single circular loop free in the cytoplasm, often with small plasmids.

questions.q: Which equation correctly gives the magnification of a microscope image?
questions.explain: Magnification is calculated as image size divided by actual size.

questions.q: A cell has a real diameter of 0.05 mm and appears 10 mm wide in an image. What is the magnification?
questions.explain: Magnification = 10 mm / 0.05 mm = 200.

questions.q: Which type of microscope is needed to see small subcellular structures such as ribosomes?
questions.explain: Electron microscopes have far higher resolution and magnification, revealing structures too small for a light microscope.

questions.q: What is the main function of the mitochondria?
questions.explain: Mitochondria are where most aerobic respiration takes place, transferring energy for the cell.

questions.q: What is the shape of a DNA molecule?
questions.explain: DNA is a polymer made of two strands coiled into a double helix.

questions.q: Which statement best defines the genome of an organism?
options: The entire genetic material of an organism
All the proteins in a cell
questions.explain: The genome is all of the genetic material (DNA) of an organism.

questions.q: Enzymes are best described as:
options: Biological catalysts that speed up reactions
questions.explain: Enzymes are biological catalysts that speed up reactions without being used up.

questions.q: In the 'lock and key' model of enzyme action, why does an enzyme only work on one substrate?
options: Enzymes are used up in the reaction
The substrate fits the active site like a key in a lock
All enzymes break down the same substrate
questions.explain: Each enzyme's active site has a complementary shape to its specific substrate, so only that substrate fits.

questions.q: Why does an enzyme stop working at very high temperatures?
options: Its active site changes shape so the substrate no longer fits
questions.explain: High temperatures denature the enzyme, changing the active site's shape so the substrate can no longer bind.

questions.q: An enzyme in the small intestine works best at pH 8. If acid lowers the pH to 3, what is most likely to happen?
options: The rate decreases as the active site changes shape
There is no effect on the rate
questions.explain: A pH far from the optimum denatures the enzyme, altering the active site and slowing the reaction.

questions.q: Which is the correct word equation for aerobic respiration?
questions.explain: Aerobic respiration uses glucose and oxygen to release energy, producing carbon dioxide and water.

questions.q: Respiration is described as an exothermic reaction because it:
questions.explain: Respiration is exothermic because it releases (transfers out) energy from glucose.

questions.q: What is produced by anaerobic respiration in human muscle cells?
questions.explain: Anaerobic respiration in animals converts glucose into lactic acid without using oxygen.

questions.q: A brewer uses yeast to ferment sugar with no oxygen present. Which products are formed?
questions.explain: Anaerobic respiration in yeast (fermentation) produces ethanol and carbon dioxide.

questions.q: Which is the correct word equation for photosynthesis?
questions.explain: Photosynthesis uses carbon dioxide and water, powered by light, to make glucose and oxygen.

questions.q: Photosynthesis is described as an endothermic reaction because it:
questions.explain: Photosynthesis is endothermic because it takes in (absorbs) light energy from the surroundings.

questions.q: Why is chlorophyll in the chloroplasts important for photosynthesis?
options: It absorbs light energy for photosynthesis
questions.explain: Chlorophyll is the green pigment that absorbs light energy needed to drive photosynthesis.

questions.q: On a bright, warm day, raising the carbon dioxide concentration increases the rate of photosynthesis. This shows carbon dioxide was:
questions.explain: Because increasing it raised the rate, carbon dioxide was the limiting factor holding photosynthesis back.
